chunks: Hammad narrated from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Takbir in the days of Tashriq after the prayer, so he said: 'The Takbir is in Mina after fifteen prayers, and in the other regions after ten prayers. And the first Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Nahr (Sacrifice), in which you say: Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamd. Allahu Akbar upon what He guided us, Allahu Akbar upon what He provided us from the beasts of grazing livestock. And the Takbir is made in the other regions after ten prayers because when the people depart in the first departure, the people of the regions refrain from the Takbir, and the people of Mina continue to Takbir as long as they are in Mina until the final departure.'

key_terms.بَهِيمَةِ اَلْأَنْعَامِ: Beasts of grazing livestock (camels, cattle, sheep)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for reciting Takbir after prayers during the days of Tashriq in Mina versus other regions?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the continuous Takbir in Mina and the restricted practice in other regions, reflecting the scholarly view that the latter is a commemoration of the former. It highlights the specific liturgical formula for the Day of Sacrifice, emphasizing gratitude for guidance and livestock, which aligns with the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' precise ritual instructions. The ruling underscores the communal unity of the Hajj while acknowledging geographical variations in ritual observance.
